name: Plaza Independencia
description: Public plaza beside Fort San Pedro in the downtown port area. The Legazpi–Urdaneta monument stands here.

steps.instruction: Walk southeast toward the port along Magallanes Street or Osmeña Boulevard.
Board 17B toward Carbon and get off at Colon.
Walk southeast toward the port.

notes: Pin is approximate; help us confirm the location.

name: Fort San Pedro
description: Triangular bastion fort beside Plaza Independencia; construction started in 1565.
entrance_fee: Reported ₱30 for adults, ₱20 for students and seniors; confirm

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and get off at Colon.
Walk southeast toward Plaza Independencia; the fort is beside it.
Board 08F toward Mambaling and get off at Colon.
Walk southeast toward Plaza Independencia; the fort is beside it.

notes: The fort was damaged in the 2025 Cebu earthquake; confirm that it is open.

name: Magellan’s Cross
description: Pavilion beside the Basilica del Santo Niño on Magallanes Street, housing the cross linked to Magellan’s arrival in 1521.
hours: Reported open at any time of day

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and ask for Colon or Carbon.
Walk, or take a short second ride, to Magallanes Street beside the Basilica.

name: Basilica Minore del Santo Niño
description: Minor basilica founded in 1565 and home of the Santo Niño de Cebu image.

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and ask for Colon or Carbon.
Walk, or take a short second ride, to the Basilica beside Magellan’s Cross.

name: Cebu Metropolitan Cathedral
description: Cathedral in the downtown heritage district near the Basilica del Santo Niño.

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and get off at Colon.
Walk toward the Basilica; the cathedral is in the same heritage district.

notes: Pin is approximate; help us confirm the location.

name: Casa Gorordo Museum
description: 19th-century ancestral house museum in the Parian district at 35 Lopez Jaena Street (also called Eduardo Aboitiz Street).

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and get off at Colon.
Walk a few minutes into Parian toward Lopez Jaena Street.

notes: Pin is approximate. Sources disagree on the fee (₱70 to ₱120) and hours (about 09:00–17:00 or 10:00–18:00, Tuesday to Sunday); confirm before going.

name: Colon Street
description: Reputed to be the oldest street in the Philippines, traced to the 1560s town plan. Today a busy downtown strip.

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon and get off at Colon.
Board 08F toward Mambaling and get off at Colon.

notes: Pin is approximate; help us confirm the location.

name: Carbon Market
description: Large public market in the old downtown, at the Carbon end of jeepney 17B.

steps.instruction: Board 17B toward Carbon, the end of the line, and say “Carbon ni?” before sitting.

notes: Pin is approximate; help us confirm the location.

name: Cebu Taoist Temple
description: Taoist temple built in 1972 by Cebu’s Chinese community in Beverly Hills, reached by an 81-step staircase, with city views.
hours: Reported about 09:00–17:00 daily (some sources say 08:00); confirm

steps.instruction: Ride 04L toward JY Square in Lahug.
Jeepneys do not enter the Beverly Hills subdivision. Take a metered taxi or ride-hailing car from Lahug to the temple.

notes: Dress modestly; sleeveless tops and short skirts may be refused entry.

name: Tops Lookout
description: Hilltop observation deck in Busay with views over Cebu City, Mandaue and Mactan.
hours: Reports vary: open 24 hours, or about 07:00–24:00; confirm

steps.instruction: Ride 04L toward JY Square in Lahug. 04L does not go up to Tops.
Continue uphill by shuttle, taxi or an agreed motorcycle ride. Agree on the fare before riding.

notes: Pin is approximate. An older listing mentions a shuttle from IT Park; confirm before relying on it.
